items.label: Include the AIClient Library
items.content:
# Including the AIClient Library

To use AIClient in browser environments, include the following script tag in your HTML. This makes the `AIClient` class available globally.

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/HyperRushNet/hrn-ai/client/1.0.3.min.js"></script>
```

### What Happens When You Load This Script
- The AIClient library is initialized in the page.
- `AIClient` becomes globally accessible.
- No module bundlers or build steps are required.

### Requirements
- Include this script **before** any code that uses `AIClient`.
- This version is only for browser environments; it is not a Node.js package.

---

items.label: Initialize the Client
items.content:
# Initializing the Client

After including the script, you must create a new client instance and provide your API key.

## JavaScript Example
```javascript
// Create a new instance of AIClient and set the API key
const client = new AIClient()
  .setApiKey('YOUR_API_KEY');
```

### What This Does
- Stores the API key internally.
- Prepares the client for requests.

### Internal Default Configuration
| Property | Default Value |
|----------|----------------|
| model | "flux" |
| type | "text" |
| systemPrompt | "You are a helpful assistant." |
| timeout | 30000 |
| retry | true |
| retryAttempts | 2 |
| retryDelay | 1000 |
| seed | null |
| width | 1024 |
| height | 1024 |
| history | [] |

### Important Notes
- The API key is required; without it, calls to `generate()` will fail.
- The client does not validate the API key; validation occurs on the server.

---

items.label: Set Text Mode
items.content:
# Set Text Generation Mode

The client must be configured for text generation before issuing text requests.

## JavaScript Example
```javascript
// Configure client to generate text output
client.setType('text');
```

### What This Does
- Configures the client to use text endpoints.
- Internally this affects the request payload and endpoint targeted.

### Endpoint Used
Text generation uses the `POST /v1/chat/completions` endpoint on the API.

---

items.label: Select a Text Model
items.content:
# Selecting a Model for Text

After setting the mode to text, you must specify which model should handle the request.

## JavaScript Example
```javascript
client.setModel('openai-fast');
```

### What This Does
- Assigns the model as a string inside client config.
- The model name is passed verbatim to the API.
- The client does **not** verify the model name.

### Model Information and Status
Models supported by the service may change over time. Visit the official model listing to explore available models and their capabilities:

👉 https://enter.pollinations.ai/#:~:text=Models

### Model Health and Availability
Model status, latency, and health stats are available here:

👉 https://model-monitor.pollinations.ai/

---

items.label: Generate Text
items.content:
# Generating Text Output

Once the client is configured for text and a model is set, you can generate text output.

## JavaScript Example
```javascript
const output = await client.generate('Explain how AIClient works');
console.log(output);
```

### What Happens Internally
1. The client prepares a JSON body containing:
   - `model`
   - `messages` (including system prompt, history, and user messages)
   - `seed` (numeric, deterministic or random)
2. It sends a POST request to the text generation API.
3. On success, it returns the generated text.
4. User + assistant messages are appended to the internal history.
5. If the history becomes longer than `2 * historyLimit`, the oldest messages are removed.

### History Management
The client stores the last messages up to the configured `historyLimit`. This supports context preservation across prompts.

### Error Conditions
| Error Condition | Result |
|----------------|--------|
| No API key | Throws Error: "API Key is required" |
| Empty prompt | Throws Error: "Input prompt cannot be empty" |
| Server error (5xx) or 429 | Retries if retry is enabled |
| Timeout | Throws "AI Request Timeout" |

---

children.label: System Prompt
children.content:
# System Prompt

You can change the system prompt, which is included as the first message in every text generation request.

## JavaScript Example
```javascript
client.setSystemPrompt('You are a knowledgeable assistant.');
```

### Default
```
You are a helpful assistant.
```

### Purpose
- Provides a role definition for the model.
- Useful for defining tone, style, or behavior expectations.

---

children.label: Request Timeout
children.content:
# Timeout Configuration

Controls how long the client waits before aborting an active request.

## JavaScript Example
```javascript
client.setTimeout(45000); // 45 seconds
```

### Behavior
- Uses the `AbortController` API internally.
- If the request exceeds the timeout, it is aborted and an error is thrown.

---

children.label: Seed (Determinism)
children.content:
# Seed for Deterministic Output

You can set a numeric seed to influence pseudo‑random generation. This helps produce repeatable outputs when all other parameters are the same.

## JavaScript Example
```javascript
client.setSeed(123456);
```

### Notes
- If `seed` is not provided, the client generates a random seed internally.
- Seed affects different models in different ways, depending on the service.

---

children.label: Retry Logic
children.content:
# Retry Logic

Configures how the client handles transient errors.

## JavaScript Example
```javascript
client.setRetry(true, 3, 1500);
```

### Parameters
| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| enabled | boolean | Whether retries are enabled |
| attempts | number | How many retry attempts to make |
| delay | number (ms) | Delay between attempts |

### Behavior
- Retries only when the API returns:
  - HTTP 429 (rate limit)
  - HTTP 5xx (server error)
- Retries are not attempted on other error codes.

---

children.label: Clear History
children.content:
# Clear Conversation History

Clears the internal chat history stored by the client.

## JavaScript Example
```javascript
client.clearHistory();
```

### Behavior
- Removes all stored historical messages.
- Does not affect other configuration parameters.

---

content.label: Select Image Model
content.content:
# Selecting an Image Model

After specifying image mode, you must choose a model capable of image output.

## JavaScript Example
```javascript
client.setModel('gptimage');
```

### Model Reference
Consult the official pollinations model page to see which models support image generation and their capabilities:

👉 https://enter.pollinations.ai/#:~:text=Models

### Model Health
Check model health, uptime, and status:

👉 https://model-monitor.pollinations.ai/

---

content.label: Image Dimensions
content.content:
# Image Dimensions

Image generation models require numeric width and height.

## JavaScript Example
```javascript
client.setDimensions(1024, 1024);
```

### Notes
- Width and height default to 1024.
- Non‑numeric values will revert to defaults.

---

content.label: Generate Image
content.content:
# Generate Image

Once configured, you can generate an image based on a text prompt.

## JavaScript Example
```javascript
const blob = await client.generate('A futuristic city skyline');
const imageUrl = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
document.querySelector('img').src = imageUrl;
```

### Internal Process
1. Sends prompt, model, width, height, seed to the image API.
2. Receives a base64‑encoded image in JSON.
3. Decodes base64.
4. Converts to a `Blob` with MIME type `image/png`.
5. Returns the `Blob`.

### Usage
- Use the `Blob` to set an image `src` or to trigger a download.

---

You can monitor model health, latency, and availability using the official dashboard:

- Observing latency and error rates.
- Making informed decisions about model selection.
